title: Understanding Regularization
text: Regularization is a technique used to prevent overfitting in models by adding a penalty term to the loss function. This penalty discourages complex models that fit the training data too closely.

title: L1 vs L2 Regularization
text: L1 regularization, also known as Lasso, adds a penalty equal to the absolute value of the magnitude of coefficients. It can lead to sparse models where some feature weights are zero. L2 regularization, or Ridge, adds a penalty equal to the square of the magnitude of coefficients, which tends to shrink coefficients evenly.

title: Choosing the Right Regularization
text: Consider the nature of the data and the problem. If there are many features but only a few are expected to be important, L1 regularization might be more suitable as it can zero out less important features.
